name: Liberal corporatism
summary: Liberal corporatism keeps a market economy and individual liberty but organises economic life through bargaining among employers, workers and the state as social partners, with minimal state direction. It treats the firm as a social institution, calls for democratising it through worker election of management, and is democratic, in contrast to authoritarian or fascist corporatism.
scope: The democratic, non-authoritarian strand: John Stuart Mill's case for labourers' associations, the progressive-era 'interest group liberalism', and post-war societal neo-corporatism in Austria, the Netherlands, Germany and the Nordic states. Excludes fascist and Catholic-corporatist variants. Most social, cultural and foreign-policy questions are not addressed by the doctrine, so those answers are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not addressed directly; the Nordic, Austrian and Dutch corporatist systems are built around extensive welfare states, so adherents lean yes (and the Dutch/German model does it through social-partner-run insurance).

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Corporatist systems set pay through sector bargaining between the social partners rather than statutory minimums, so a substantial legal rise is not the preferred route; inferred from the bargaining model.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Liberal corporatism does not reject markets and Mill defends competition, but it adds organised coordination; markets are the base mechanism, not a claim of superiority over all government action.

public-ownership.rationale: Mill's ideal is workers' associations owning capital and the sources stress firms as social institutions in markets, not state ownership of industry.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Sources say nothing on tax rates; Nordic corporatist states tax heavily while Mill-style liberals were cautious, so adherents are split.

unions-good.rationale: Strong labour unions are one of the 'social partners' in neo-corporatism and Mill treats worker associations as good for workers, though liberal corporatists want them integrated into bargaining rather than adversarial.

property-fundamental.rationale: Mill rejects confiscation yet foresees capital becoming joint property of workers; protection of property is accepted but not held as near-absolute, so split.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Firms are treated as social institutions that must recognise members' needs, which implies obligations; but 'more tightly' is not stated, so inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: The corporatist welfare states (Nordic, Austrian, Dutch) are comprehensive; the polder model supported an extensive welfare state even while trimming it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Mill expects labourers' associations collectively owning capital with elected managers to predominate, and liberal corporatism calls for democratising the firm; but some forms are non-socialist, so not strong.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; liberal-democratic corporatists are split between security and civil-liberty concerns.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No documented position; adherents spread across the liberal-democratic mainstream.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: No documented position; European corporatist states often restrict it while the Millian liberal strand resists, so split.

strong-leader.rationale: Consensus bargaining among organised partners and coalition government (polder model) is the opposite of bypassing gridlock through one leader; neo-corporatism is defined against top-down fascist corporatism.

state-harmful.rationale: Neo-corporatism depends on the state recognising and working with social partners; it is a democratic, state-engaging model.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not an issue the doctrine addresses; no basis for either side.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No documented position; Dutch and German corporatist states legalise it but the doctrine itself is silent.

decide-locally.rationale: Liberal corporatism favours decisions at the sector and national level among peak bodies, not primarily local ones, though subsidiarity appears in Catholic corporatist roots; inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the liberal-democratic and Nordic penal tradition.

traditional-family.rationale: Catholic corporatism stressed family but liberal corporatism is secular-liberal and silent; split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal-democratic outlook and the practice of Nordic and Dutch corporatist states.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the liberal-democratic outlook of these states.

more-religion-public.rationale: Liberal corporatism is liberal and its model is organised around economic interest groups rather than churches; inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the mainstream liberal-democratic outlook of corporatist states.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Some forms have nationalist-liberal traits (German State Party) but the mainstream is silent; split.

gradual-change.rationale: Consensus bargaining and incremental concertation (polder model) work through established institutions and avert disruption.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: No stated view; the model is organised nationally, though its states are often pro-EU, so split.

free-trade.rationale: Small open corporatist economies depend on trade; the polder article notes Dutch trade dependence ruled out protectionism.

nation-first.rationale: Trade-dependent corporatist states favour cooperation; inferred from the Dutch case.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; social-partner systems tied to national labour markets make eventual open borders unlikely to be endorsed.

limit-growth.rationale: Concertation aims at employment and growth (Wassenaar deal sought jobs); degrowth is not part of it.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The doctrine concerns industrial organisation, not technology; adherents hold no shared view on whether progress solves most problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No documented view; energy policy is outside the doctrine.

revolution-justified.rationale: Liberal corporatism arose partly as a reaction against syndicalism and rests on consensus; Mill seeks a spontaneous, non-confiscatory transition.

experts-over-public.rationale: Polder concertation relied on expert planning advice (Central Planning Bureau) but is also organised democratic representation; split.

central-planning.rationale: Mill champions competition and liberal corporatism does not reject markets; it seeks bargaining within markets, not central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: The doctrine accepts markets with firms run by or answerable to workers; Mill's co-operative associations compete in markets, though non-socialist forms exist.

land-value-tax.rationale: Mill favoured taxing unearned land increment, but the corporatist tradition is silent; split.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Mill favoured limiting inheritance but the doctrine is otherwise silent; split.

basic-income.rationale: Corporatist welfare is built on work-linked, contributory social insurance negotiated by partners; an unconditional income is inferred as foreign.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Open trade economies; inferred from Dutch trade dependence.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State intervention is minimal in sector bargaining; investment steering is not part of the model.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Mill favours wide worker ownership via associations, which broadly spreads property; but not the doctrine's focus.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The model is market based and Mill's associations still pay wages and profits; abolition is outside it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Market-based but state-engaging systems; no support for abolishing state institutions.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Organised social partners bargain over economic policy and wages, with minimal state intervention; the statement adds state recognition and price-setting, which goes beyond what liberal corporatism specifies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Neo-corporatism is explicitly democratic as opposed to fascist or one-party state corporatism.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Constitutional monarchies (Netherlands, Nordics) host corporatist systems but the doctrine is indifferent; split.

democracy-best.rationale: Neo-corporatism is presented as a democratic form of corporatism; the doctrine also supplements majority rule, which keeps it from +2.

direct-votes.rationale: Corporatism sees majority-rule voting as marginalising specific interests and prefers negotiated representation; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Workers should vote on management but political power stays with parliament; councils replacing parliaments is not the doctrine.

right-to-secede.rationale: The model is built on national-level bargaining bodies in unified states, so a right of regions to leave is inferred as unwelcome.

natural-rulers.rationale: Mill's liberal egalitarianism about labourers' self-government cuts against hereditary rulers; inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: Concertation and consensus aim at avoiding conflict, but absolute pacifism is not stated.

war-builds-character.rationale: A consensual, liberal outlook; inferred as rejecting militarist claims.

separate-church-state.rationale: Catholic corporatism influenced the broader tradition but the liberal strand is silent; split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Liberal corporatism is a liberal-democratic doctrine; scriptural law is not part of any described version.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The model centres on state-recognised bodies and a state partner; privatising law and defence is far from it.

military-superiority.rationale: Small corporatist states such as the Netherlands and Nordics seldom claim superiority over rivals, but nothing in the doctrine decides it.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nationalist-liberal traits exist in some forms but ethnic homogeneity is not a doctrine; inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: It replaces class conflict with cooperation between partners and arose as a reaction to syndicalism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Mill aims at equalising labourers' standing, not outcomes; inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Nothing in liberal corporatism concerns indigenous land; adherents would be split along ordinary liberal lines.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The doctrine is silent on colonial history; adherents spread across the liberal-democratic mainstream.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from national-level bargaining.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Mill defends competition but also cooperation; split.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Corporatism stresses social roles of firms but liberal corporatism does not reject individualism.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is outside the doctrine, which is about organising economic interests.

limit-population.rationale: Concertation aims at employment and growth, and the doctrine has no population policy; coercive limits are inferred as unwelcome to liberals.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Mill and the corporatists build on industrial economies; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Consensus bargaining aims to manage change through established partners, so disruption of institutions for speed is inferred as unwelcome.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not an issue the doctrine addresses; liberal adherents would split between freedom and caution.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Negotiated representation among organised groups is the model; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Digital privacy is not discussed; liberal-democratic adherents would split between liberty and security.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Polder pragmatism puts consensus and results ahead of doctrine; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Concertation aims at averting strikes and disruption.

means-match-ends.rationale: Nothing stated; the doctrine's own practice is negotiated reform, but it makes no general claim about means and ends.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The doctrine resembles Taylorism with democratised management; division of labour assumed.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Mill and the model retain market rewards; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The doctrine does not reject markets, and Mill sees profit-sharing and partnership, not exploitation theory.

collective-farming.rationale: Mill favoured co-operative association but also peasant proprietors; inferred.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not stated; liberal doctrine accepts markets.

taxation-theft.rationale: Welfare-state corporatist systems rely on taxes and contributions.

harm-principle.rationale: Mill authored it but the corporatist tradition does not claim it; split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Corporatism gives organised groups a representative role; rights are not individual only.

conscription.rationale: Several corporatist states use it, others have abolished it; the doctrine is silent.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Voice through organised bargaining is the core mechanism.

state-as-business.rationale: Firms are social institutions; the state is not a business.

positive-liberty.rationale: Mill's labourers' self-dependence suggests enabling freedom; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: The model locates power in organised economic partners and the state, not in universities or media; inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Interest representation through trade bodies; but liberal corporatism keeps parties and parliament, so only agree.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal personal fealty is the opposite of democratic, institutionalised partnership among representative bodies.

bound-labor.rationale: Mill rejects hereditary dependence of labour.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Mill's liberal rationalism assumes knowledge can be pursued impartially; the stance is inferred as sceptical of this claim.

universal-morality.rationale: Mill's utilitarian liberalism assumes reasoned moral standards; the corporatist tradition itself is silent so this is inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Corporatist bargaining balances organised interests rather than a single common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not a question the doctrine addresses; adherents are split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not a question the doctrine addresses; adherents are split.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is outside the doctrine; adherents are split.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Calls for democratisation of the firm and election of management by workers; Mill's managers elected and removable.

school-vouchers.rationale: Dutch and Nordic corporatist states fund private and religious schools, yet the doctrine takes no view on vouchers; split.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Polder model combined with budget cuts; not stated for stimulus; split.

economic-freedom.rationale: Markets are preserved but the doctrine is not stated in these terms.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nationalist-liberal traits exist in some forms, but the doctrine has no stated position on nation-states.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal institutionalism.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Christian-democratic corporatists sit beside secular liberals, so adherents are split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare is linked to contribution and residence in these states, but the doctrine does not address immigrants; split.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Contributory welfare is work-linked but conditionality is not stated.

class-collaboration.rationale: Social partners cooperate; core of the doctrine.

dominated-front.rationale: Open, trade-dependent corporatist states are integrated with Western powers and would not join an anti-Western front.

workers-nation.rationale: The doctrine seeks class cooperation within the nation rather than organised class politics, national or international.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Liberal adherents would reject legal gender roles; corporatist states of the Nordic type are strongly egalitarian.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Neo-corporatism treats the state as one partner.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy supply is outside the doctrine; split by national circumstances.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Corporatist states differ greatly, from Dutch integration policy to Nordic multiculturalism; split.

proportional-representation.rationale: Coalition consensus in PR systems; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: A consensual, small-state model with no claim to spread its system by mission; inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Institutionalised partnership implies trust in institutions; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: A liberal-democratic rule-of-law outlook implies accountability for abuses; inferred.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts liberal equality of persons that Mill's tradition upholds; inferred.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate with no connection to the doctrine.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; adherents split.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; corporatist states differ on religious law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Mill's liberalism defends freedom of belief; restriction is inferred as rejected.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religious demand with no home in a liberal market-based doctrine.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Christian-democratic and secular strands of corporatism differ, as the Dutch pillarised schools show; split.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Leninist theory of the socialist state, opposed to the democratic character of neo-corporatism.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; Dutch export reliance but no mercantilist doctrine.

population-transfer.rationale: A liberal-democratic doctrine opposed to authoritarian state corporatism would reject forced removal of minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A libertarian absolutism not held by corporatists, who accept state coercion for taxes and bargaining frameworks, though they are not militarists either; split.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Mill defends competition but social Darwinism not adopted; split.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Several corporatist democracies (Germany, Austria) have such laws while others do not; the doctrine takes no stance.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Mill's rejection of the employer-employed hierarchy resonates.

separated-powers.rationale: Neo-corporatism sits within liberal-democratic constitutions, which usually separate powers; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Neo-corporatism is a democratic system of voluntary social partnership, and liberal corporatism arose against syndicalist and revolutionary currents, so a revolutionary leading party has no place.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Welfare-state corporatism protects workers broadly through insurance rather than giving the poor first priority; split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure is outside the doctrine; adherents split by party.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Concertation aims at avoiding strikes yet depends on union strength; split.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Mill's cooperative argument locates poverty in social arrangements of labour, not population alone; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The Nordic and Dutch consensus models rest on liberal institutions rather than ethnic homogeneity; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The model relies on representative organisations choosing delegates, not sortition; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Corporatist bargaining sometimes fixes prices, but the doctrine favours markets; adherents split.

party-commands-army.rationale: A feature of authoritarian single-party states, contrary to neo-corporatism's democratic character.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation is not discussed by the doctrine; corporatist states differ.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Nothing in the doctrine favours capping politicians' pay at a worker's wage; inferred as disagree.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; liberal parties vary.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Corporatist small states are pro-EU; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Parliamentary coalition systems typical of corporatist states place command with the government; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Christian-democratic corporatism has Catholic roots but the liberal strand is indifferent to church governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Religious rule contradicts the democratic liberal character of the doctrine.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist slogan; corporatists seek class cooperation, including in wartime.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Mill's liberalism of free expression rejects moral censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from liberal-democratic constitutionalism that favours checks on incumbents.

recall-officials.rationale: The model works through stable representative institutions, not mid-term recall; inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Trade-dependent small corporatist states, such as the Netherlands, are NATO and EU members; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: A market-accepting doctrine has no basis for abolishing renting.

people-in-arms.rationale: Replacing professional forces with an armed citizenry is alien to this institutional doctrine.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Corporatism is about industrial and sectoral organisation of labour, not rural romanticism; inferred.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Expert-informed concertation (Planning Bureau) values educated advice; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: No documented view; adherents split between relativist and universalist liberals.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Liberal-democratic Nordic and Dutch corporatist states teach it; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Mill's rationalist liberalism and modern corporatist states reject it; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; split between liberal and Christian-democratic strands.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Corporatist states vary (Germany versus Netherlands); the doctrine has no view.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill authored this; the corporatist tradition silent.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A Marxian dependency claim; corporatists favour reform within markets, so inferred as disagree.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Neo-corporatism is explicitly democratic as opposed to authoritarian state corporatism.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Nordic and Dutch corporatist states are generous aid donors; inferred from practice.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not addressed; most corporatist states have none, but the doctrine is silent.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Wage restraint and price stability go together in the Dutch and German model; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Firms as social institutions suggests some agree.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A left-theoretical debate unconnected to the doctrine.

collective-defense.rationale: The main corporatist states are NATO members; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not addressed; Christian-democratic and secular strands disagree.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Constitutional monarchies and presidents above party are normal in these states; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Sacred rulers belong to the pre-liberal and fascist traditions that neo-corporatism rejects.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Welfare-state corporatist systems use progressive taxation; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The model is democratic, rule-of-law and constitutional.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is far from the doctrine, which concerns bargaining over economic organisation; adherents have no shared view.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Corporatist proposals for second chambers exist, but the statement is not addressed.

leader-cult.rationale: A fascist-corporatist trait; neo-corporatism is the democratic contrast.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine; corporatists reject class struggle, so inferred as disagree.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentism is contrary to the consensual, liberal-democratic model; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Mill's liberty principle makes the demand contrary to liberal values.

common-currency.rationale: Open trade-dependent corporatist states such as the Netherlands and Austria joined the euro; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic unions are not discussed in the sources; adherents would be split.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Corporatist ideas of group self-organisation resemble this, but not stated; split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The sources give no view on minority emigration versus struggle for rights; adherents split.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A Marxist thesis; not discussed by corporatists.

no-bailouts.rationale: Dutch concertation was paired with privatisation and cuts yet bailout policy is not stated; split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Neo-corporatism sits within liberal-democratic constitutions; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not addressed; Nordic practice leans yes but doctrine is silent.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Open trade dependence is a precondition of the Dutch consensus model.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Social partners would favour labour standards in trade agreements; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: The doctrine accepts markets and material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Opposed to revolution and armed vanguards; the model is consensual.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Curriculum content is outside a doctrine about economic bargaining; adherents split.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Mill held a paternalist view but modern adherents; split.

patriotic-education.rationale: Some forms have nationalist-liberal traits but the mainstream strand takes no view on patriotic schooling.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is not addressed by the doctrine; adherents split along liberal lines.

public-money-creation.rationale: A market-accepting doctrine has no stated case for public money creation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Doctrine premised on adapting capitalism by bargaining.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Imperial legacies are not discussed in the sources; no basis for a stance.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Corporatism sees workers in rich countries as partners in a shared system, not as beneficiaries of extraction; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Welfare-state corporatism and liberal egalitarianism reject it; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Corporatist states differ on constitutional entrenchment, and the sources do not address it.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: A post-colonial question outside the doctrine; adherents split.

elective-rulers.rationale: Democratic doctrine opposed to hereditary rule; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Corporatist consensus style resembles it but is not stated.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Neo-corporatism assumes a lawful democratic order and says nothing on resistance rights.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not addressed; interest-group bargaining shares lawmaking influence.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The doctrine assigns duties to firms as social institutions, but not a paternalist duty of the wealthy; split.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The model relies on citizens organising into representative bodies.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not part of a liberal-market doctrine.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The doctrine rejects the ruling-class model of the state.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Open trade is accepted as beneficial; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: A debate among communist parties with no counterpart in liberal corporatism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Small trade-dependent states favour integration; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revanchism is contrary to the consensual model.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Neo-corporatism defines itself against fascism, but the constitutional claim is not addressed.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Neo-corporatism defines itself against fascist corporatism but takes no stated view on equating fascism with communism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: A culture-war question the doctrine does not address; adherents split.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender policy is outside the doctrine; adherents split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The doctrine presents democratic corporatism as the alternative to authoritarian versions; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Nordic states fund care services but the doctrine itself does not address paying domestic work.

filial-duty.rationale: Family obligations are not addressed by this economic doctrine; adherents split.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service recruitment is not addressed; adherents split.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from liberal-democratic corporatist states' practice.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Delegates in bargaining bodies are mandated, but the doctrine uses stable representatives; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Mill accepts private property in land, though with reforms; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy is outside the doctrine, and corporatist states range from monolingual to multilingual.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A legal-theory question outside the doctrine; adherents split.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The doctrine accepts markets without judging consumption; adherents split.

corporate-influence.rationale: Interest group liberalism accepts group lobbying; split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed; open-economy adherents might lean no, but the doctrine does not decide.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Nordic family policy includes such incentives but the doctrine takes no view; split.

job-guarantee.rationale: Nordic active labour-market policy resembles it but the doctrine is silent.

democratic-peace.rationale: Liberal internationalism of these states; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Neo-corporatism relies on lawfully recognised bodies; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Sectoral bargaining suggests industrial unions but not stated; split.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy claims are contrary to the democratic liberal tradition.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Welfare corporatist states link benefits to family law; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Nordic states have strong freedom-of-information laws; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Opposed to informal organisation: organised, licensed bodies.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Small EU states accept supranational law; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Corporatist welfare states pool resources nationally; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Property in means of production is accepted in markets, and personal property is not in dispute, so there is no meaningful stance.

defeat-communism.rationale: Cold-war strategy is not part of the doctrine; adherents range from anti-communist to coexistence.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Dutch and German systems deliver publicly funded services through private and non-profit providers; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Mill accepts the progress of competitive industry while seeking association; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; adherents split between reformist and structural views.

socialized-care.rationale: Nordic public care exists but the doctrine is silent.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism has no place in an open, trade-oriented liberal doctrine, so adherents lean disagree.

treaties-binding.rationale: Minority treaty rights are not discussed in the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Mill favours cooperatives within markets rather than communities of common property.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Corporatism often presents itself as a third way.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Competing historical land claims are not addressed; adherents split.

holocaust-denial.rationale: A factual claim rejected by liberal-democratic adherents.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Neo-corporatism is democratic, opposed to authoritarian suppression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Contrary to Mill's freedom of opinion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Mill criticised exploitative colonial rule; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious-legal question outside liberal corporatism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Workplace participation yes, but broader not stated.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: A critical-theory claim the doctrine does not address; adherents split.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Gender recognition is not addressed by the doctrine; adherents split.

assisted-dying.rationale: A bioethical question with no basis in the doctrine; Dutch law permits it but adherents differ.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Corporatism is sometimes presented as a third way, but not stated; split.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxian concept; the doctrine's democratisation of the firm responds to similar concerns but is not framed that way.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; secular and Christian-democratic strands differ.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A workplace-law question the sources do not discuss; adherents split.

social-market-economy.rationale: Germany's social market economy is listed as a neo-corporatist form.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine is about organised bargaining within existing economies.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Corporatist states are split between NATO members and neutrals such as Austria and Sweden historically.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Constitutional monarchies host corporatism but are indifferent.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not addressed; Dutch wage restraint was a domestic bargain, not conditions from lenders, so no clear stance.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist claim outside the doctrine.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Media ownership is not addressed by the doctrine; adherents split.

online-participation.rationale: Digital democracy is not addressed; the doctrine centres on organised bodies.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents split.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The model favours organised representative bodies over random assemblies; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Doctrine is silent on religious reform; adherents split.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Mill worried about the hereditary employer-employed divide, but the claim is not stated; split.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The model relies on state institutions.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Corporatist welfare states provide aid through public social insurance.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed; the doctrine concerns interest representation.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not addressed; the doctrine favours bargaining through bodies.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: No stated view; the doctrine is not about long-term risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Internal church governance is outside the doctrine; adherents split.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Mill's liberalism supports equality in marriage; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The doctrine is silent; some corporatist states allow it, others do not.

rent-control.rationale: Housing regulation is not addressed; adherents split between social-market and neutral views.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Defence basing is not addressed; adherents split.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between NATO supporters and others.

recognise-genocide.rationale: A historical-politics question outside the doctrine.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Mill's profit sharing rewards labour; unclear.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The doctrine is a modern liberal-democratic arrangement of economic interests, not a myth of ancient national continuity; inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: A feminist-theory question outside the doctrine.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Sacralising national martyrs belongs to nationalist and fascist traditions that neo-corporatism contrasts itself with; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The consensus-seeking, interest-bargaining view treats politics as negotiation, not a struggle between good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: A Zionist-theory question outside the doctrine.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Territorial unification of peoples is not addressed.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The doctrine is partly non-socialist, and the question belongs to socialist debates.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Nordic and Dutch states often run local utilities publicly, but the doctrine takes no stance.

second-chamber.rationale: Corporatist second chambers exist as proposals but not stated.

municipal-property.rationale: Mill favours worker associations and private markets, not municipal ownership of production; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The model coordinates through national or sector bodies, not local assemblies; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Union-bargained family wages were part of mid-century corporatist deals, but the doctrine does not state it; split.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Regulatory policy is outside the doctrine.

person-over-state.rationale: Mill's liberalism gives primacy to persons; liberal corporatism does not reject individualism, per its Wikipedia description.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Christian-democratic and secular strands differ; no common view.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Territorial constitutional design is not addressed.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural technology is outside the doctrine.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning is outside the doctrine.

communal-electorates.rationale: Representation by group occurs in corporatist bodies, but separate religious electorates would conflict with a unified democracy; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: A conspiratorial claim with no basis in a consensus doctrine; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Nordic states offer it but the doctrine does not address tuition.

capital-controls.rationale: Dutch and Austrian economies depend on open trade and finance, so controls on capital are inferred as unwelcome.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: A state recognised as a partner in democratic bargaining presupposes a monopoly of force; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The doctrine works within lawful institutions and does not endorse refusal of orders; inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Collective bargaining is the core mechanism; sector bargaining central.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax-credit design is not addressed; wage bargaining is the preferred tool.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Neo-corporatism needs a functioning state as one of the partners in tripartite bargaining, so smashing it is the opposite of the model.

sacred-nation.rationale: Sacralising the nation is a fascist-corporatist trait contrasted with the democratic neo-corporatist model; inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: A regional-dependency theory outside the doctrine.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Philosophical anthropology is not addressed; adherents split.

public-service-media.rationale: Dutch and Nordic states fund public broadcasters, but the doctrine is silent on media policy.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Religion is outside the doctrine, which is an economic bargaining model; no inference possible.

farm-price-support.rationale: Neo-corporatist systems incorporate farm organisations as social partners and the Dutch and Nordic states have supported agriculture; inferred from tripartite practice in s2 and s4.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Defence is not addressed by the doctrine; the small corporatist states it cites mostly rely on alliances, giving no clear lean.

workers-own-party.rationale: Corporatism seeks cooperation among classes through social partnership, closer to broad parties covering all classes than to a separate workers' party; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: A liberal, democratic doctrine protecting individual liberty would accept a ban on bodily harm; not addressed in the sources.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The doctrine keeps individual liberty and equal civil rights under a market economy, so equal property rights are the natural reading; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; the sources give no signal.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Corporatism favours negotiated, institutionalised regulation among social partners and the state over leaving matters to private suits; inferred from the bargaining model.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Liberal corporatism gives formal roles to economic interest groups, not traditional leaders, and is democratic; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Environmental trade-offs are not addressed; the doctrine keeps individual liberty but accepts negotiated regulation.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: A liberal, consensus-oriented doctrine leans toward judicial discretion; inferred, as sentencing is not addressed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The Dutch and Nordic states cited as models expect integration including language; the doctrine itself is silent, so inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Liberal corporatism rests on voluntary association and individual liberty, while Mill defends free associations of labourers, so compelled membership sits uneasily; however, social-partner systems often rely on strong union coverage, so this is inferred.

voter-id.rationale: The doctrine does not address election rules; adherents in the Nordic, Dutch and Austrian systems differ on this.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from its liberal pluralism and non-authoritarian character, which sets it against Catholic-corporatist state religion; not discussed in the sources.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The sources stress that liberal corporatism is democratic, in contrast to authoritarian and fascist corporatism, which fits a procedural view though the doctrine also adds social-partner bargaining beyond elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to individual liberty; the sources do not address sexual morality.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The doctrine is liberal and democratic and values individual liberty; inferred, the sources do not discuss shutdowns.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Corporatist welfare states rely on sector bargaining and social insurance run by the social partners rather than a single state cash payment; inferred from the Dutch and Nordic models.

women-suffrage.rationale: Liberal corporatism is democratic and liberal, and the Nordic, Dutch and Austrian systems it describes grant women full political rights; Mill also argued for it.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; inferred from its liberal, secular-leaning character that adherents would not blame religion as a main cause.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from its liberal outlook; the doctrine does not address race.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The Nordic, Dutch and Austrian systems it draws on have equality ministries and ombuds; inferred, the sources do not discuss them.

missingStatements.text: Employers' associations and trade unions should negotiate pay and economic policy at sector or national level with the government as a partner.
missingStatements.rationale: This tripartite or sector bargaining is the central mechanism of neo-corporatism.

missingStatements.text: Firms should be run as social institutions that answer to their workers as well as their owners.
missingStatements.rationale: Liberal corporatism treats the firm as a social institution that must recognise members' needs.

notes: Wikipedia's article is a short stub, so documented positions concentrate on economic organisation; most other answers are inferred from the liberal-democratic character of the corporatist states.
